## Highlights since 0.20.1

- **Overleaf's "too many requests" waits as long as Overleaf asks, and says so.** In the native Lattice, when Overleaf answers live sync with "too many requests", the cool-down now lasts as long as Overleaf asks, between 30 seconds and 5 minutes, instead of a fixed guess. While it waits, the Overleaf status in the title bar reads Overleaf asked to wait, retrying in N s, and the waiting sync goes out the moment the cool-down ends instead of on the next check up to 45 seconds later. Error messages for such an answer say how long to wait, in English and Chinese. Live sync also no longer asks Overleaf for its latest version a few seconds after it has just read it.
- **Export review PDF says which document a note belongs to.** In the native Lattice, when Export review PDF… opens on a PDF that doesn't contain some notes' document, a banner names that document, such as "1 note is in main.tex, which this PDF does not show.", instead of marking each note Not on this PDF with no reason. On the live PDF the banner has Build main.tex, which builds that document and places the notes again once its PDF is on screen.
- **Saving an included Typst file builds the whole document.** In the native Lattice, in a Typst project with no main document set, ⌘S or an autosave on a part that another `.typ` file includes now builds the document that includes it, through any number of levels. Before, the part was compiled alone and its PDF replaced the document's, and with no main document at all the part became the project's main document.

## Notable fixes

- In the native Lattice's visual view, a `\colorbox` with one of xcolor's named colours, such as `\colorbox{yellow}{…}`, is now filled like an `[HTML]` colour, and its text stays readable on the fill (#1327).
- Typing in a `.tex` file's visual view in the native Lattice takes less CPU: it no longer asks TexLab again for a word that had no completions a moment before. On a 240 KB paper, CPU while typing fell from about 20% to 15%.
- The Agent panel's provider banner shows plain text instead of raw colour codes when Lattice was started from a shell that forces colour, and a warning saved by an earlier run no longer appears at startup as if it were current.
- In a Chinese interface, the native Lattice gives the reasons a live Overleaf connection timed out in Chinese.
- A folder too shallow to give to the Agent is now refused with "The Agent can only be given a folder at least three levels deep.", in English and Chinese, instead of a message about the home folder.
